s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest and back pain with electrocardiogram changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers, suggesting an acute cardiac syndrome
salient_findings: Diffuse ST-segment depression and ST elevation in lead aVR on electrocardiogram
Elevated cardiac troponin I level of 620 pg/mL
Diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle on transthoracic echocardiography
Cystic mass above the left atrium on contrast-enhanced CT scan
key_facts: 63-year-old woman
History of hypertension
Chest discomfort and dyspnea on exertion for two months
Sinus rhythm with occasional premature ventricular complexes on electrocardiogram
Elevated cardiac troponin I level of 620 pg/mL
Diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle on transthoracic echocardiography
Cystic mass above the left atrium on contrast-enhanced CT scan
Mass had heterogeneous attenuation (15–56 Hounsfield units) on noncontrast images
Mass exhibited slight contrast enhancement
Transient cardiogenic shock that responded to noradrenaline support

raw.rationale: The presence of a cystic mass above the left atrium with heterogeneous attenuation and slight contrast enhancement on CT scan, along with symptoms of chest discomfort, dyspnea, and elevated cardiac troponin I level, suggests a left atrial myxoma obstructing blood flow and causing cardiac symptoms.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The presence of a cystic mass and the specific location above the left atrium do not align with typical findings of acute myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: Cardiac tamponade
rejected.why: There is no mention of a significant pericardial effusion, which is a hallmark of cardiac tamponade.

rejected.label: Pericardial cyst
rejected.why: The mass's location above the left atrium and its heterogeneous attenuation with contrast enhancement are not typical for a pericardial cyst.

rejected.label: Cardiac metastasis
rejected.why: While possible, the description of the mass and the clinical presentation do not strongly suggest metastasis without further evidence of primary cancer.
